story.title: The Water's Lying
story.premise: In 2197, Piq Ansari-Holm, a Ceres-born field officer of the Ledger, the intelligence service of the Ceres Hydrological Compact, boards the Aldrin cycler Aubade under her genuine cover as a certified auditor for the Interplanetary Habitability Board. Ceres sells the water that shields every crewed ship in the inner system. Her mission is to assess, and if ordered to disable, the Umbrella, a prototype superconducting magnetic radiation shield that could make water shielding obsolete. She also has to learn how her predecessor aboard died. Teodor Vasz's last message read only 'The water's lying.' The Umbrella's lead physicist is Dr. Hana Szelig, brilliant, defensive and openly contemptuous of auditors. Piq's sign-off can end Hana's life's work. During the five-month fall to Mars the two women circle each other through audits, secrets and an amateur shipboard play. Piq then discovers that the ship cannot stop, cannot easily change course, and has quietly spent much of its shielding water as propellant. The shield she was sent to destroy may be the only thing that keeps 220 people alive through a solar storm. To save them, Piq has to choose between her service, the truth, and the woman she has fallen for, using information that is always minutes or hours out of date.
story.setting: The inner solar system in 2197, near solar maximum. Almost all of the action takes place aboard the Aubade, a Tharsis Transit Aldrin cycler on the 146-day fast leg from Earth flyby to Mars flyby. It carries about 90 crew and 130 passengers and researchers. The ship has a non-rotating central hub containing the storm shelter, wrapped in hub water tanks that were originally about 8,000 tonnes and are the bulk of its shielding. It also has a 120-metre-radius ring spinning at 1.68 rpm to give Mars-normal 0.38 g, with thinner shielding, the farm decks and the cabins. The spin axis is held sunward so that the main solar array on the sunward hub cap stays lit. Small electrothermal thrusters burn water as propellant, so every trajectory correction is paid for in shielding. The Umbrella coil is mounted around the hub, and its dipole axis lies along the spin axis. The Aubade cannot stop. People can only join or leave it by high-g taxi rendezvous at planetary flybys. Ceres is near solar conjunction from the ship's point of view, so Ledger traffic travels through Mars-trailing relays that store and forward messages. Delays run from about 40 minutes to many hours, and the relay headers are stripped for security. Light-speed delay, delta-v budgets, dose limits, heat rejection and the moment of inertia of a spinning ship are the everyday terms of the story. Politically, Ceres's water monopoly is under pressure from the Mars Directorate and the Lunar Consortium, and Tharsis Transit is a Mars-chartered carrier running near insolvency.
story.tone: Close third person on Piq throughout, with no head-hopping. The reader learns only what Piq perceives, calculates or misjudges, which is what makes the twists fair. Prose is vivid but economical: concrete sensory detail of spin gravity, hub microgravity, recycled air, frost on coolant lines and the ache of Ceres-born bones under 0.38 g, with no purple passages and no lectures. Physics comes through action and Piq's quick mental arithmetic: delays, dose budgets, delta-v, torque. Each chapter runs about 4,000 to 5,000 words and ends with forward momentum, such as a new fact, a decision forced, a signal arriving or a clock starting. The comedy is regular and situational and grows from the setting and the characters: the captain's forty-page welcome protocol, a loose hen in microgravity, an elderly passenger casting a real spy as a fictional spy, tomato bribes for the feared auditor, the 'Schrödinger's auditor' limbo while a suspension notice crawls through light-delay, and a bug that fails but exposes something better. Comedy recedes completely at the tensest moments, so the storm, the EVA and the revelation about Teodor's death are played straight. The romance is a true slow burn of professional friction, grudging respect, shared secrets, a rupture and a chosen reconciliation, and it is always tied to the plot. Every twist reframes earlier scenes from clues already shown on the page. None of them is a betrayal, and Hana never betrays Piq.

characters.name: Piq Ansari-Holm
characters.role: Protagonist. A 34-year-old Ledger field officer whose cover is a real Interplanetary Habitability Board auditor credential. Born in Ceres's 0.03 g, she is clumsy and aching on the ring but moves through the microgravity hub with the ease of a native.
characters.want: To finish Teodor's work, find out who killed him, and earn her way home to Ceres by proving she is still the Ledger's best. Underneath that, she wants to be known by someone as she really is.
characters.flaw: She lies so fluently that she has stopped noticing when she does it. She trusts numbers and procedure over people, cannot ask for help, and confuses obedience with integrity.

characters.name: Dr. Hana Szelig
characters.role: Love interest. A Mars-born plasma physicist who leads the Umbrella active-shielding project aboard the Aubade. She is not an agent of anyone and never betrays Piq.
characters.want: To prove that active shielding works, so that no one else dies the way her younger brother Tomas did: leukemia after a solar storm caught Phobos Station's thin shelters.
characters.flaw: Certainty that slides into recklessness. She runs unlogged tests to dodge oversight she considers cowardly, and she hides her failures rather than share them.

characters.name: Teodor Vasz (deceased)
characters.role: The Aubade's former water quartermaster and Piq's predecessor as Ledger asset aboard. He died during an EVA on the long loop, and his death was ruled a tether failure. He appears through his logs, his margin notes and the objects he left behind.
characters.want: In life, to prove that the ship's shielding water records were false before anyone was hurt.
characters.flaw: He was too secretive to ask for a safety spotter on a covert EVA, and that secrecy helped kill him.

characters.name: Sabine Okoro
characters.role: Piq's Ledger handler on Ceres. She is present only through delayed, compressed messages.
characters.want: To protect Ceres's people and economy as water's monopoly ends, without losing her officers.
characters.flaw: Her caution and compartmentalisation produce orders that make sense when sent and can be monstrous when they arrive.

characters.name: Lucan Ferro
characters.role: Antagonist. Tharsis Transit's Director of Operations aboard the Aubade. He is openly management, not anyone's secret agent.
characters.want: To keep the Aubade on schedule and the company solvent, and to keep a costly trajectory error from ever reaching the Board.
characters.flaw: He gambles other people's safety on optimistic projections and treats concealment as competence.

characters.name: Captain Maelis Odum
characters.role: The Aubade's master. Decent, exhausted, author of the forty-page welcome protocol, and eventually Piq's ally.
characters.want: To run a clean, safe, by-the-book ship and retire without an inquiry.
characters.flaw: She hides behind procedure when a decision frightens her, and needs three signatures to be brave.

characters.name: Ambrose Tull
characters.role: Comic lead. An 81-year-old Lunar retiree and amateur playwright who is directing this transit's traditional passenger play, 'Dead Drop at Perihelion'. He is convinced someone aboard is following him.
characters.want: To stage a triumphant spy farce and to find out who is tailing him.
characters.flaw: A theatrical paranoia that makes him right for all the wrong reasons.

characters.name: Junie Tull
characters.role: A hub rigger and EVA technician who becomes Piq's practical ally and her partner on the climactic EVA. She is Ambrose's estranged granddaughter and the person who has been following him.
characters.want: To work up the courage to speak to the grandfather she hasn't seen in twelve years.
characters.flaw: She avoids every emotional confrontation and would rather climb outside the hull than have a hard conversation.

characters.name: Osei Brandt
characters.role: Communications officer. Patient, pedantic and fond of relay queue statistics. He is the source of several fair clues about delay and about the ghost contact.
characters.want: For someone, anyone, to appreciate store-and-forward protocol.
characters.flaw: He dismisses anomalies that don't fit a known category, logging them as 'debris' and moving on.

story.arc:
ACT ONE: BOARDING (Ch 1-8). Ch 1: Piq endures a 3 g taxi rendezvous with the Aubade at Earth flyby, rehearsing her cover through grey-out. On arrival she receives Captain Odum's forty-page welcome protocol and is assigned Teodor's old cabin. Hana meets her with a hostile, colour-tabbed binder. Alone, Piq replays Teodor's last message, 'The water's lying', and finds a scratched tally of dates on the cabin's locker. Ch 2: The audit begins. Piq is clumsy in ring gravity and graceful in the hub. Hana's contempt sharpens. Teodor's EVA file shows he died on the hub truss near the coil housing, and his kit inventory is missing a steel torque wrench (CLUE, Twist 3). Ambrose drafts Piq into his play. The chapter ends with her covert receiver catching its first encrypted-looking burst. Ch 3: Piq inspects the storm shelter. It sits on the spin axis behind the hub tanks, below the sunward solar array (CLUE, cusp). Her dosimeter reads background above spec, and the crew call it a calibration drift (CLUE, Twist 2). The hub lights flicker at 02:00, at the same time as a burst (CLUE, Twist 1). A hen named Admiral escapes into the hub during a shelter drill. Piq concludes there is a mole aboard. Ch 4: Osei explains conjunction-season relay queuing and the stripped headers. Piq does her delay arithmetic assuming a 34-minute standard (CLUE, Twist 4). Sabine's orders arrive: Disposition A is to observe, Disposition B is to disable. Piq and Hana clash over quench protection, and a first spark passes between them when Hana describes auroras to a woman who grew up under no sky. That night Piq picks the lock of the dark lab and is caught in the corridor by Ambrose rehearsing. Ch 5: A comic mole hunt. Piq suspects Osei and Ambrose. Her microgravity bug fails, but it trips a ventilation fault that exposes Ferro and Odum arguing about an unpublished 'trim budget' (CLUE, Twist 2). A stuck spin-transfer elevator forces Piq and Hana into their first honest conversation. Another burst comes at 02:13, and Hana is yawning the next morning (CLUE, Twist 1). Piq finds her own name in Ambrose's notebook beside the word 'SPY?'. Ch 6: The notebook turns out to be casting notes. Ambrose wants her to play an auditor who is secretly a spy, and she has to accept to protect her cover. Teodor's quartermaster logs have been replaced. Propellant burns outnumber the published burns, and the Mars arrival time on the schedule board has slipped forty seconds (CLUE, Twist 2). Hana shows Piq the dipole field diagrams, and Piq quietly notices the polar cusps (CLUE, cusp). In Teodor's margin she finds 'D/H?' (HOOK SEED). She decides to stake out the hub at 02:00. Ch 7: On the night hunt, Osei mentions an unidentified long-range radar return that he has logged as debris (HOOK SEED). Piq finds Hana alone at the coil console just as a burst fires. Ch 8, TWIST 1: There is no mole. Hana demonstrates that the bursts are quench-protection pulses from her secretly energised coil, modulated by the solar wind and picked up by Piq's broadband receiver. The flickering lights, Hana's exhaustion and the burst timestamps were all physics. Hana has been testing illegally under pressure from Ferro. Piq does not report it, and this is her first complicity. The chapter ends with Hana asking: 'That's my crime. What's yours?'

ACT TWO: THE WATER (Ch 9-16). Ch 9: Intimacy grows through zero-g stage-combat rehearsals and tomato bribes from crew who fear the auditor. Junie says the hub tanks 'sound hollow' when she raps them (CLUE, Twist 2). Sabine replies: if the test is live, prepare Disposition B. Ch 10: Piq designs a sabotage that would force a controlled quench, ruining the coil without injuring anyone. Osei mentions that conjunction backlogs can stretch to hours (CLUE, Twist 4). Sabine's messages begin to sound anxious about the price of water (HOOK SEED). Hana tells Piq about Tomas. Piq's guilt builds through a comic hygiene audit of the composting bay. She borrows Junie's neutron moisture gauge, the same model Teodor used. Ch 11: The hub tanks read 54 percent. Teodor's gauge log places his final EVA at the tank exterior beside the coil housing at 01:58 (CLUE, Twist 3), and his saved readings include an isotopic flag (HOOK SEED). Ferro catches Piq and locks her out of the logs with velvet menace. Ch 12, TWIST 2: Piq reconstructs what happened. A taxi docking mishap during the last Earth flyby perturbed the ship's trajectory, and Ferro secretly spent about 45 percent of the hub shielding water as propellant to make the Mars flyby. He is gambling on the Umbrella being ready before solar maximum. The water was lying. The shield Piq was sent to kill is the safety margin for 220 people, and the high dosimeter readings, the hollow tanks, the trim budget and the forty seconds all make sense. The chapter ends on her dilemma: reporting the truth to Ceres means telling Ceres that the ship is vulnerable. Ch 13: Using her real auditor's authority, Piq tells Odum, who retreats into procedure. Piq sends the full report to Sabine. Hana is furious with Ferro and terrified of her own coil. The two women nearly kiss. Ferro files a complaint asking the Board to suspend Piq's authority. Ch 14: Comic dueling bureaucracies follow. While the suspension crawls through light-delay, Piq is a 'Schrödinger's auditor', and crew sort themselves by which unarrived message they believe. Hana explains the cusp risk, which she had classed as theoretical (CLUE, cusp). Piq spots Junie tailing Ambrose. Archived burst logs show a burst at 01:58 on the night Teodor died. Ch 15: With Junie, Piq retraces Teodor's EVA path and finds his torque wrench embedded in the coil housing's thermal blanket, pulled there by the fringe field. Ch 16, TWIST 3: No one murdered Teodor. Hana's unlogged coil ramp yanked the ferrous wrench, which severed his tether and breached his suit while he was secretly gauging the tanks. Ferro covered up an accident to avoid an inquiry, not a killing. The murder Piq came to avenge was a collision between Ledger secrecy and Hana's rule-breaking. Piq tells Hana. She also confesses that she is Ledger. Hana tells her to get out.

ACT THREE: THE STORM (Ch 17-24). Ch 17: Hana self-reports to Odum and wants to shut the Umbrella down, the one thing keeping everyone safe. Using rehearsal as cover, Piq argues her back to her console. Ambrose and Junie edge toward each other. Disposition B arrives: execute before the Mars flyby. Piq believes it is Sabine's answer to her report. Ch 18: Piq refuses B and tells Hana all of it. They reconcile and kiss in the hub's observation blister under the zodiacal light. Osei reports an X-class flare. The light has arrived and the particles are behind it. Ch 19: The countdown starts, with prompt protons expected within the hour and the CME shock in about thirty hours. Piq notes a relay artifact on the B message but has no time to do the arithmetic (CLUE, Twist 4). Hana's simulation shows that with the spin axis held sunward, the Umbrella's cusp would face down the Parker-spiral particle stream and funnel the flux into the axial shelter. Running the shield as configured would kill the people it was built to protect. Ch 20: The only fix is to precess the ship's spin axis about fifty degrees off the Parker-spiral line. That costs propellant, which means burning more of the remaining shielding water and committing everyone to an untested shield. Odum's three-signature rule meets Ferro's refusal, and Piq's suspended authority is restored by a Board reversal that happens to arrive in time. A propellant valve is stuck in the hub, and someone has to go outside under the first proton flux. Ch 21: Piq and Junie make the EVA on strict dose budgets while Hana ramps the coil. Ferro tries to abort, and Odum relieves him of duty. The precession burn tips the axis. The shock arrives early and the coil approaches a quench. This chapter contains no comedy. Ch 22: Through the storm peak, 220 people crowd the shelter, Hana nurses the coil by hand and Piq's dose climbs. The Umbrella holds. Then Sabine's later message arrives, saying her report was received, Disposition B is to be disregarded, and lives come first. TWIST 4: Piq works out the timing. Through the conjunction queue, B was sent before her report reached Ceres. Sabine was never willing to kill them. Piq made her choice blind, and the choice stands. The flux falls, and the coil quenches cleanly as the storm ends. Ch 23: In the aftermath, Piq has mild radiation sickness, the Board opens an inquiry, Ferro is removed, and Teodor's death record is corrected. Hana formally testifies to her role and will answer for it before the Board. Piq and Hana decide together to publish the Umbrella flight data openly to every power so that no one can monopolise it. Ambrose's play goes on in the hub, Admiral the hen is finally caught on stage, and Junie and Ambrose reconcile. Osei confirms that the 'debris' is a warm, crewed-signature object outbound toward Jupiter with no water mass. Piq opens Teodor's isotopic file. Ch 24: At the Mars flyby, the taxi to Deimos is waiting. Piq receives Sabine's summons to Ceres, and Hana is offered a Board-protected seat to stay with the coil on the long loop. Piq and Hana choose each other, give up their separate paths, and board the same taxi together toward a hearing, a summons and a future neither can calculate. Main arc, central mystery, romance and every subplot are closed.

Deliberate trilogy hooks, left open on purpose: (1) Ceres's reckoning. Sabine's summons and the Compact's response to openly published active shielding leave open what Ceres will do as its water monopoly collapses, and whether Piq returns to the Ledger as hero, defendant or something else. (2) The ghost ship. An unregistered, crewed vessel carrying no water shielding is outbound toward Jupiter, which implies someone already flies with working active shielding. It is seeded in Ch 7 and Ch 14 and confirmed in Ch 23. (3) The heavy water. Teodor's 'D/H?' note and his isotopic readings show that the Aubade's remaining shielding water is deuterium-enriched, meaning someone has been smuggling fusion fuel through cycler tanks. Who did it, and for whom, is left open. It is seeded in Ch 6 and Ch 11 and revealed in Ch 23.
subplots: The death of Teodor Vasz. Piq investigates what she believes is a murder covered up by management, and finds the truth: an accident caused by Hana's unlogged coil test while Teodor was on a covert EVA. It is resolved when the record is corrected and Hana testifies to her role (Ch 2-16, closed in Ch 23).

The water drawdown. Ferro secretly spent shielding water as propellant to fix a trajectory error and gambled on the Umbrella being ready. Piq exposes it, Ferro is relieved during the storm, and the Board inquiry and his removal close the thread (Ch 3-12, closed in Ch 21-23).

Piq's loyalty to the Ledger. She is ordered to prepare and then execute sabotage, refuses, and learns through the conjunction delay that Sabine had already rescinded the order. Her choice and her relationship with Sabine are resolved. The wider question of Ceres's response is a deliberate hook (Ch 4-22).

Hana's guilt and her brother Tomas. Her grief drives her recklessness, and Teodor's death breaks her. She chooses to keep the shield running, saves the ship, and accepts accountability rather than hiding her failure (Ch 10-23).

Ambrose Tull's play, 'Dead Drop at Perihelion'. Piq is cast as an auditor who is secretly a spy, and the rehearsals give her cover, comedy and private conversations with Hana. The play is performed in the hub after the storm (Ch 2-23).
Ambrose's tail. The man who believes he is being followed is right: Junie, his estranged granddaughter, has been following him. They reconcile on opening night (Ch 5-23).
Admiral the hen. A running microgravity gag, she escapes into the hub during drills and at inconvenient moments, and is finally caught on stage during the play (Ch 3-23).
Captain Odum's procedural paralysis. She hides behind protocol and three-signature rules, then finds the courage to relieve Ferro and authorise the precession burn (Ch 1-21).
Piq's body. As a Ceres-born woman aching under 0.38 g, she weighs whether she could live anywhere but home. Choosing the Deimos taxi with Hana is also choosing to live in a heavier world (Ch 1-24).

outline.summary: A 3 g taxi rendezvous with the Aldrin cycler Aubade at Earth flyby. Piq Ansari-Holm, Ceres-born and built for 0.03 g, rehearses her cover through grey-out: she is a genuinely certified Interplanetary Habitability Board auditor. Her true employer is the Ledger, the intelligence service of the Ceres Hydrological Compact. The mission is to assess the Umbrella, a prototype superconducting magnetic radiation shield that threatens Ceres's water monopoly, and to disable it if ordered. She must also learn how her predecessor, water quartermaster Teodor Vasz, died. On arrival, Captain Maelis Odum presents her forty-page welcome protocol with real pride, including a mandatory initials page and a section on correct handrail etiquette. Piq's ring-gravity stumbles at 0.38 g ache in her Ceres bones. She is assigned, coolly, to Teodor's old cabin. Dr. Hana Szelig, the Umbrella's lead physicist, meets her at the spin-transfer elevator with a colour-tabbed binder of pre-emptive rebuttals and open contempt for auditors who 'end programs by signature'. Piq is fluent, charming and lies so easily she barely notices. Alone, she replays Teodor's last message, 'The water's lying.' She finds a scratched tally of dates hidden on the inside of the cabin locker. The final mark matches the day of his fatal EVA.

The audit begins. Piq lurches through the ring's Coriolis drift, spilling tea sideways, and then glides through the non-rotating hub like a native. A rigger notes this with suspicion. Hana answers every question with a page reference and nothing more. Piq inspects the storm shelter. It sits on the spin axis, wrapped in the hub water tanks and directly below the sunward solar array and the spin axis held toward the Sun. Her personal dosimeter reads background above spec, and the crew wave it off as calibration drift. Teodor's EVA file says he died on the hub truss near the Umbrella coil housing and rules it a tether failure. His kit inventory is missing one steel torque wrench, which nobody has remarked on. In the commissary, the 81-year-old Lunar playwright Ambrose Tull, who is directing the traditional passenger play 'Dead Drop at Perihelion', insists Piq has 'a face for intrigue'. He drafts her before she can refuse, and he complains that someone aboard is following him. That night Piq's covert broadband receiver, tuned for Ledger traffic, catches its first encrypted-looking burst from somewhere inside the ship.

At 02:00 the hub lights flicker in the same second her receiver logs another burst. Piq notes the timestamp and reads it as a transmitter drawing power. During a shelter drill, a farm hen named Admiral escapes into the hub. She tumbles in microgravity, the drill collapses into a chase, Odum consults the protocol for livestock, and Piq catches the bird one-handed in a move no ring-born auditor should know. Communications officer Osei Brandt, delighted that someone is listening, explains conjunction-season store-and-forward through Mars-trailing relays. Ceres is behind the Sun from the ship's position, and headers are stripped for security. Piq does her delay arithmetic on the standard 34-minute assumption and files it as settled. Sabine Okoro's compressed orders arrive. Disposition A is to observe. Disposition B, held in reserve, is to disable the Umbrella. Piq decides that the bursts mean a mole: another agent aboard, reporting to someone else. She picks the lock of Hana's darkened lab that night. Ambrose catches her in the corridor, rehearsing his villain's monologue at the bulkhead, and assumes she is 'getting into character'.

A comic mole hunt. Piq suspects Osei, who has an obsessive interest in queue statistics, and Ambrose, whose paranoia looks like tradecraft. She plants a microgravity bug in a ventilation junction. It fails completely, but it trips a fault that carries voices down the duct: Director of Operations Lucan Ferro and Captain Odum arguing about an unpublished 'trim budget' that Odum refuses to sign without two more signatures. Piq and Hana clash bitterly over the coil's quench protection. Then a spin-transfer elevator jams between ring and hub, and they are stuck together in shifting partial gravity for an hour. Their first honest conversation happens there. Hana describes auroras on Mars to a woman who grew up with no sky, and something passes between them that neither acknowledges. Another burst comes at 02:13, and the next morning Hana is yawning through a briefing. In the rehearsal room, Piq finds Ambrose's notebook with her own name written beside the word 'SPY?'

The notebook turns out to be casting notes. Ambrose wants Piq to play an auditor who is secretly a spy. Refusing would draw more attention than accepting, so she accepts, and gets notes from Ambrose that she is 'too obviously lying'. Back at work, she finds that Teodor's quartermaster logs have been replaced with clean versions. Her cross-check against thruster telemetry shows more propellant burns than the published schedule allows. On the schedule board, the Mars flyby arrival time has slipped forty seconds without explanation. Hana, thawing slightly, shows Piq the Umbrella's dipole field diagrams. Piq quietly notices the polar cusps, the funnels where field lines converge along the axis, and says nothing. In a margin of Teodor's paper backup log she finds 'D/H?', written in his cramped hand. She cannot place it. She decides to stake out the hub at 02:00 and catch whoever is transmitting.

Piq's night hunt through the hub. Osei is on the late watch and mentions, in passing, an unidentified long-range radar return. It is too warm for a rock and has no transponder, and he has logged it as debris because it fits no category. Piq follows a frost-rimed coolant line to the coil console and finds Hana there alone just as her receiver fires. TWIST 1: there is no mole. Hana, cornered, demonstrates that the bursts are quench-protection pulses from her coil, which she has been secretly energising. The solar wind modulates them, and Piq's broadband receiver picked them up as noise that looked encrypted. The 02:00 flicker was the coil's power draw, and the yawning came from night after night of unlogged tests. The burst timestamps were physics, not spycraft. Hana admits Ferro has been pressuring her to prove the shield works before Mars. Piq does not report it, and this is her first complicity. Hana studies her: 'That's my crime. What's yours?'

Piq deflects Hana's question with a lie she half believes. Their intimacy grows anyway, through zero-g stage-combat rehearsals that Ambrose choreographs badly and they redo properly, all elbows, momentum and laughter. Frightened crew start leaving hydroponic tomatoes at Piq's cabin door as bribes for the feared auditor, and the pile becomes absurd. Junie Tull, a hub rigger, mentions that the hub tanks 'sound hollow' when she raps them on inspection rounds. Sabine replies to Piq's report on the coil: if the test is live, prepare Disposition B. Piq designs a sabotage that would force a controlled quench and ruin the coil without hurting anyone, and she hates how elegant it is. Osei grumbles that conjunction backlogs can stretch to many hours, not minutes. Piq half-listens. Sabine's next message is oddly anxious about the falling price of water on the Mars exchange. The chapter ends with Piq's sabotage plan finished and stored.

In the observation blister, Hana tells Piq about her younger brother Tomas. He died of leukemia after a solar storm caught Phobos Station's thin shelters, and the Umbrella exists so that no one else dies that way. Piq's guilt sharpens through a comic hygiene audit of the composting bay, where the farm crew have staged an elaborate cleanliness performance and Admiral the hen sabotages it on cue. Piq borrows Junie's neutron moisture gauge, the same model Teodor used, and gauges the hub tanks covertly. They read 54 percent. The gauge's memory still holds Teodor's last session, which places him at the tank exterior beside the coil housing at 01:58 on the night he died. The saved readings carry an isotopic anomaly flag she does not understand. Ferro intercepts her in the logs office and locks her out of the systems, all courtesy and velvet menace, with a reminder that auditors are guests. Piq walks away holding the gauge and knowing the numbers will not wait.

TWIST 2. Piq reconstructs what happened from the pieces she already has. A taxi docking mishap during the last Earth flyby perturbed the Aubade's trajectory. To make the Mars flyby, Ferro secretly spent about 45 percent of the hub shielding water as electrothermal propellant. He is gambling that the Umbrella will be ready before solar maximum. The water was lying. The dosimeter's 'drift', the trim budget Odum would not sign, the forty-second slip and the hollow-sounding tanks all click into place. The shield Piq was sent to kill is now the safety margin for 220 people. Then the dilemma lands. Reporting the truth to Ceres means telling a water power that a Mars-chartered ship is vulnerable. Staying silent means betraying her service. Piq invokes her real auditor's authority, and the cover becomes the most honest thing she has. She lays the numbers before Odum, who retreats into procedure and asks for three signatures. Piq then sends the full report to Sabine and watches it vanish into the conjunction queue.

Hana learns about the drawdown. She is furious with Ferro and, for the first time, terrified of her own coil. Alone in the dark lab, she and Piq nearly kiss and pull back. Ferro files a complaint asking the Board to suspend Piq's authority. Since neither the complaint nor any ruling can arrive for hours, Piq becomes a 'Schrödinger's auditor'. Crew sort themselves by which unarrived message they believe: some stop greeting her, some double the tomatoes, and Odum issues a memo addressing her as 'Auditor (provisional)'. Hana explains the cusp risk, the flux funnelling along the dipole axis, which she had classed as theoretical because the shield's design assumed a different geometry. Piq notices Junie trailing Ambrose through the ring at a distance. Osei mentions that the debris return is still there and is moving. Combing archived receiver data, Piq finds a burst logged at 01:58 on the night Teodor died.

Piq and Junie suit up and retrace Teodor's EVA path across the hub truss. Junie climbs like someone avoiding a conversation indoors, and Piq moves with the ease of microgravity. At the coil housing they find his steel torque wrench embedded in the thermal blanket, dragged there by the fringe field. TWIST 3: no one murdered Teodor. He was secretly gauging the tanks without a spotter at 01:58 when Hana's unlogged coil ramp yanked the ferrous wrench out of his grip. It severed his tether and breached his suit. Ferro hid the accident to avoid an inquiry, not a killing. The murder Piq came to avenge was a collision between Ledger secrecy and Hana's rule-breaking. Back inside, Piq tells Hana the truth about the wrench. Then, with nothing left to hide behind, she confesses that she is Ledger. Hana tells her to get out.

Hana self-reports her role in Teodor's death to Odum and demands that the Umbrella be shut down, the one thing protecting everyone aboard. Piq cannot reach her through official channels, so she uses rehearsal as cover. On a darkened stage, in her role as the auditor-spy, she argues that hiding a failure and abandoning a shield are the same cowardice, and she gets Hana back to her console. Ambrose and Junie edge toward each other: a shared meal, an aborted sentence, Ambrose suddenly sure his tail has a familiar walk. Then Disposition B arrives: execute before the Mars flyby. Piq believes it is Sabine's answer to her report, that Ceres has read the numbers and still wants the shield dead. She sits alone in Teodor's cabin with her finished sabotage plan.

Piq refuses Disposition B and goes to Hana with everything: the orders, the sabotage plan, Sabine, the lie she has lived. They reconcile in the hub's observation blister under the zodiacal light. The kiss is chosen and earned. Osei calls urgently: an X-class flare. The light has arrived, and the particles are behind it, with prompt protons expected within the hour and the CME shock in about thirty. Rushing to the bridge, Piq notices a relay artifact in the B message's metadata but has no time to do the arithmetic. Hana's emergency simulation shows that with the spin axis held sunward, the Umbrella's cusp would face down the Parker-spiral particle stream and funnel the flux straight into the axial storm shelter. Running the shield as configured would kill the people it was built to protect.

Piq and Hana work out the only fix: precess the ship's spin axis about fifty degrees off the Parker-spiral line. Piq runs the torque and moment-of-inertia arithmetic in her head. The cost is propellant, which means burning more of the remaining shielding water and committing everyone to an untested shield. Odum's three-signature rule meets Ferro's flat refusal. Piq's suspended authority is restored by a Board reversal that happens to arrive in time, and its arrival is played without comedy, as a thin piece of luck. Then a propellant valve in the hub sticks. Someone has to go outside under the first proton flux to free it. Junie volunteers immediately, Piq insists on going with her, and they work out strict dose budgets. The chapter ends with them sealing their helmets as Hana begins ramping the coil.

This chapter contains no comedy. Piq and Junie work the stuck valve on the hub exterior with dosimeters climbing and frost on the coolant lines. They count minutes against sieverts. Hana ramps the coil, and the two women keep their tools tethered and nonferrous with Teodor's death in mind. Ferro tries to abort the burn and recall them. Odum, finally choosing courage over procedure, relieves him of duty. The valve frees and the precession burn tips the axis. The CME shock arrives early. The coil approaches a quench while Piq and Junie are still outside, and the chapter ends with them scrambling for the airlock.

Through the storm peak, all 220 people crowd the shelter. Hana nurses the coil by hand at the console, and Piq's accumulated dose climbs past her budget. The Umbrella holds. Then Sabine's later message arrives: report received, disregard Disposition B, lives come first. TWIST 4: now Piq has time for the arithmetic. With the relay artifact and Osei's warnings about hours-long backlogs, she works out that B was sent before her report ever reached Ceres. Her 34-minute assumption had been wrong all along. Sabine was never willing to kill them. Piq made her choice blind, and it stands. The flux falls, and the coil quenches cleanly as the storm ends.

In the aftermath, Piq has mild radiation sickness. The Board opens an inquiry, Ferro is removed, and Teodor's death record is corrected. Hana formally testifies to her role and will answer for it before the Board. Together, Piq and Hana decide to publish the Umbrella flight data openly to every power, so that no one can monopolise it. Ambrose's play goes on in the hub. Admiral the hen is finally caught on stage, and Junie and Ambrose reconcile on opening night. Osei confirms that the 'debris' is a warm object with a crewed signature, outbound toward Jupiter and carrying no water mass. Then Piq opens Teodor's isotopic file. The Aubade's remaining shielding water is deuterium-enriched, which means someone has been smuggling fusion fuel through cycler tanks. Who did it, and for whom, she cannot yet say.

At the Mars flyby, the taxi to Deimos is waiting. Piq receives Sabine's summons to Ceres. Hana is offered a Board-protected seat to stay with the coil on the long loop. They choose each other, give up their separate paths, and board the same taxi together, toward a hearing, a summons and a future neither can calculate. Choosing Deimos is also Piq choosing a heavier world. The main arc, the mystery of Teodor's death, the romance and every subplot are closed. Three questions stay open on purpose: what Ceres will do as its water monopoly ends, who is flying the ghost ship, and who smuggled the heavy water.
